name: Bear Crawl
description: The bear crawl is a locomotion-based functional exercise in which the athlete moves forward on hands and feet with the knees hovering a few centimeters above the floor, maintaining a flat back and neutral spine throughout the movement. It trains contralateral limb coordination, shoulder and hip stability under load, and deep core anti-extension strength. The bear crawl is widely used in athletic performance preparation, rehabilitation, and functional movement screen corrective programming.

execution.starting_position: Begin on hands and knees (quadruped) with the knees lifted to hover approximately 2–5 cm above the floor. Wrists under shoulders, knees under hips.
execution.setup_instructions: No equipment required. Adequate floor space needed for crawling distance.
steps: Step 1: Begin in the hovering quadruped position with knees 2–5 cm off the floor.
Step 2: Move the right hand and left foot forward simultaneously, maintaining a flat back.
Step 3: Follow with the left hand and right foot (contralateral pattern).
Step 4: Keep the hips level — do not let them rise or rotate as you move.
Step 5: Continue crawling forward for the prescribed distance while maintaining form throughout.
execution.breathing_instructions: Breathe continuously throughout. Do not hold breath.
common_mistakes: Letting the hips rise — the torso and hips should remain at a consistent, level height
Moving ipsilateral limbs (same-side hand and foot) — the pattern must be contralateral
Dropping the knees to the floor between steps
safety_considerations: Wrist discomfort is common for those with limited wrist extension — use fist position or push-up handles if needed.
Start with slow, deliberate movement before increasing pace.
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Consistent knee hover. Full forward reach on each hand step.
execution.tempo_recommendations: Typically 10–20 meters per set. Slow for quality, faster for conditioning.
